items.title: Wellman Braud Interview, 1958-03-31
items.q: That boy is a shock, he's a great drummer too, the one drop paid, Brunus boy.

ctx.x: But you made it. Oh, well, I can fix him that out. I didn't enjoy it so well. The first records I didn't enjoy them so well because I'm overplaying. See, the method teach you to not overplay this. And if you don't go by the method, you'll go right, because the man that wrote it, he wrote it right. Well you can tell from them records, you can tell the difference. That's moving. But you see, you have a good swing drummer, you've got a good piano player, you've got the beat. Dixie Lamb is just a beat. It's like the…

If there's anything else you want to hear, otherwise, anytime you want to go, we can drive back. That boy is a shock, he's a great drummer too, the one drop paid, Brunus boy. Oh yeah. That'd be Brunus. Or some drummer. I can tell you about drummers.

That kid turned New York upside down. Who's that boy from the Orleans play with Reed Allen? He's some drummer too. I don't know. He make them fellas like Cozy Cozy and them sound bad. Zooty, if that play sound bad, they make them sound awfully bad. Who is, when was this, recently? Oh, he was a drummer. That guy's a drummer.
